name: Oil Sponge 80
notes: A sponge loaded with oil paint, pounced on Masonite — one of nine coverage-graded members (10%..90% of core-band stroke pixels inked; the ragged edge zone is excluded from the grade by design, so measure's box coverage reads a little lower). Math: docs/fractal-texture-math.md. Tip synthesis + calibration: tips/oil-sponge.spec.json via tools/fractal-tip.mjs; spectral verification: tools/spectrum-audit.mjs. Architecture: the texture rides the DUAL slot — a spectrally shaped fractal sponge mask (pore knee ~8.5 cycles/diameter, torn vignette, per-level ink fraction) gates a solid hard round primary. The mask multiplies the finished stroke once, so its pore labyrinth survives however densely the primary accumulates; carrying the texture on the primary tip was tried first and rejected — a ~4-deep union averages the labyrinth into granular dust. Dual size 130% puts mask features across the stroke edge, which is where the ragged, texture-driven edge comes from. Rejected along the way: scatter 1.5 and 0.9 mask trains (load-clumping beads at 1-2.5 diameters; see the clumping law in the math doc §3) and narrow mask plateaus (tear bays aligned and broke the 80-90% strokes). The audit shows no stamp comb, no spectral spikes, anisotropy under 3 dB across the family. Heavy coverage breathing through scattered pore clusters.
